name: 15e adamw two steps
title: AdamW scales each step by the size of recent gradients
subtitle: θ0 = 0.5, η = 0.01, β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.95, λ = 0.1, gradients 2.0 then 0.5

steps.caption: Step 1 sees a gradient of 2.0, meaning the loss rises when θ rises, so θ should fall.
Both running averages start at 0. m = 0.1 × 2.0 = 0.2 and v = 0.05 × 2.0² = 0.2, both far too small because they began at zero.
Bias correction divides by 1 - 0.9 = 0.1 and 1 - 0.95 = 0.05, giving m̂ = 2.0 and v̂ = 4.0, the true size of the first gradient and of its square.
The ratio m̂ / √v̂ = 2 / 2 = 1.0. On the first step Adam moves every parameter by exactly η whatever its gradient size.
Decoupled weight decay subtracts η λ θ = 0.01 × 0.1 × 0.5 = 0.0005 directly. θ = 0.5 - 0.01 - 0.0005 = 0.4895.
Corrections divide by 0.19 and 0.0975, giving m̂ = 1.2105 and v̂ = 2.0769, so the ratio is 1.2105 / 1.4412 = 0.8400. The gradient fell fourfold but the step only by 16 percent.
After decay of 0.000490, θ = 0.480611. Momentum kept the step close to the earlier direction and size.

Plain gradient descent with the same η moves θ to 0.48 then 0.475. Multiply both gradients by 100 and it jumps to -2.0, while AdamW lands on the same 0.4806, since the ratio cancels the gradient scale.
